paras: The shooting into the Essex Dargan house took place near Bennettsville, in Marlboro County, South Carolina, at the end of April 1888, when a number of men fired into the home of a Black man whose son was jailed for killing a white youth and killed a three-year-old child. The son, Dock Dargan, was not harmed by the men; a wire dispatch said several attempts had been made to lynch him, while the local paper spoke only of rumors. He was hanged at Bennettsville that September.

According to the Bennettsville Democrat, Wm. E. Coxe Jr., Lucein Odom and Eugene Coxe were going to bathe at McDaniel's mill when Dock Dargan, a "colored boy" and son of "the well-known Essex Dargan," met them at the dam with a double-barreled shotgun. After "a few hurried words," the paper said, Dargan fired and killed Coxe, who was in his twentieth year, then ran toward his home; he was arrested on Sunday morning and jailed. The Democrat added that Dargan had quarreled with one of the Coxe boys before and that his mother had then brought him the same gun.

A tribute in the Southern Christian Advocate gave a different setting, saying Coxe was shot on the public road near McDaniel's Pond while returning from Bennettsville, with hardly time for a greeting. The Yorkville Enquirer later dated the killing to 28 April.

A dispatch from Bennettsville reported that "Several attempts have been made to lynch him" and that the sheriff kept the jail guarded. The Democrat, by contrast, wrote that "Rumors of lynching are heard" and that the sheriff would protect the prisoner until court met in June. On Monday night, according to the Democrat, "some parties" went to Essex Dargan's house and fired into it, "it is supposed, purposely to kill the father," but killed a three-year-old child instead. The dispatch described the attackers as "a number of enraged men" and said the whole section was aroused.

No arrest, inquest or charge against the men who fired into the house appears in the coverage. Dock Dargan, aged 19, was hanged in the Bennettsville jail on 14 September 1888 for Coxe's murder; no report of his trial was found. The Yorkville Enquirer reported that he told the sheriff he wanted only to be hanged at once and that he died of strangulation within twenty minutes, while the Savannah Morning News said his neck was broken.

The episode reached readers mainly as a wire paragraph that first ran in the Savannah Morning News on 7 May and then in regional news columns such as the Oxford Eagle's "Southern Gleanings" and the Charlotte Messenger's "Through Dixie." That paragraph called Dargan "the murderer" who had "deliberately shot" Coxe and reported the child's death in a single sentence, with no comment on the shooters. The Hillsboro Recorder shortened it further, so that the shooting into the house became "a row" in which a child was killed.

The fullest account was local: the Bennettsville Democrat, reprinted by the Anderson Intelligencer, gave the setting, named the companions, and called the dead child "innocent." The Methodist tribute in the Southern Christian Advocate mourned Coxe as "brutally murdered" by "a young negro boy," left out the child, and declined further comment because the accused was in custody. When Dargan was hanged, the Columbia dispatch ran under heads such as "TO HEAVEN VIA THE GIBBET" and "Another Hanging," with no mention of the lynching attempts or the child.

The wire dispatch reported several attempts on the jail, the Hillsboro Recorder a single failed effort, and the local Democrat only rumors of lynching. Names for the dead youth varied from W. E. Cox Jr. to "William F. Coxe," "Will C. Cox" and "Willie N. Coxe," and the Advocate's "Saturday, the 30th of April" conflicts with the Enquirer's 28 April.

reader.title: Shooting into the Essex Dargan house
bases: After talk of or attempts at lynching a jailed Black youth, a number of men fired into his father's house at night and killed a three-year-old child; it was one household, not a wider community (A1, A2).

The Bennettsville Democrat (A2) and a separate Bennettsville dispatch (A1) agree that men fired into Essex Dargan's house and killed a three-year-old child, though they differ on whether lynching was attempted or only rumored.

accounts.label: Bennettsville dispatch (wire)
accounts.gist: Dargan 'deliberately' killed Coxe; several attempts were made to lynch him while the sheriff guarded the jail, and enraged men shot into his father's house and killed a three-year-old child.

accounts.label: Bennettsville Democrat (local paper)
accounts.gist: After 'a few hurried words' at McDaniel's mill dam Dargan shot Coxe; there were only 'Rumors of lynching'; on Monday night parties fired into Essex Dargan's house, supposedly to kill the father, and killed a child.

accounts.label: Southern Gossip brief
accounts.gist: One effort to lynch Dargan failed, and 'a row ensued' at his father's house in which a child of three was killed.

accounts.label: Methodist tribute to Coxe
accounts.gist: Coxe, on his way home from Bennettsville, was shot without warning by 'a young negro boy'; the writer declines further comment because the accused is in custody.

framing.detail: The dispatch called Dargan 'the murderer' who 'deliberately shot' Coxe and closed 'The entire section is aroused', reporting the child's death without comment on the shooters.
The Bennettsville Democrat called the dead child 'an innocent three-year-old' and noted the sheriff's pledge to protect the prisoner, while calling Dargan 'the murderer'.
The Hillsboro Recorder's brief turned the shooting into the house into 'a row'.
The Southern Christian Advocate called Coxe 'brutally murdered' and said nothing of the child, but held back comment because the accused was 'in custody of the proper authorities'.
The hanging ran under heads such as 'TO HEAVEN VIA THE GIBBET', 'Died with Good Intentions' and 'Another Hanging', none mentioning the lynching attempts or the child.

record_check.dossier: mob_assault: men fired into one family's house and killed a child; no wider community was attacked.
House fired into on Monday night, about 30 April 1888, after Coxe's killing on 28 April and Dargan's Sunday arrest.

record_check.record: Dock Dorgar, Dock Dargan, a child of Essex Dorgar, ... (five variants)
record_check.dossier: One victim killed: the unnamed three-year-old child of Essex Dargan. Dock Dargan was the accused and the object of lynching talk or attempts, not a victim killed by the mob.
Black: the child of Essex Dargan, father of 'a negro boy' / 'a colored boy'.

record_check.record: said to have shot and killed a white boy (Dock Dorgar, Black boy)
record_check.dossier: Dock Dargan was accused of shooting W. E. Coxe Jr.; the household fired into was not accused of anything (the Democrat says the mother had once brought him the gun in an earlier quarrel).
1 death from the mob's action (the child); Coxe's death is the alleged crime, and Dargan's hanging on 14 September was a legal execution.
Lynching attempts or threats at the jail and shooting into a house; no pursuit or siege is reported.
Dock Dargan was not lynched (attempted or only rumored); the person killed was a child in the house the men fired into.
Dargan was in the jail; the child killed was not sought by anyone.

info: Coxe shot on Saturday, 28 April 1888 per A19 (A11 says 'Saturday, the 30th of April'); Dargan arrested Sunday; the house fired into on Monday night (A2), 'last night' in the dispatch printed May 7 (A1).
Coxe killed near the east end of the dam at McDaniel's mill (McDaniel's Pond), near Bennettsville; the shooting was at the home of Essex Dargan near Bennettsville.

An unnamed three-year-old child in the house of Essex Dargan, father of the accused, was killed; the Democrat says the shots were 'supposed' meant for the father. Dock Dargan, the jailed accused, was the object of lynching talk or attempts but was not harmed.
Dock Dargan, a 'negro boy', was accused of shooting and killing W. E. Coxe Jr., a white youth, with a double-barreled shotgun.
'a number of enraged men' (A1); 'some parties' (A2); not named and race not stated.
Dock Dargan, aged 19, was hanged in the jail at Bennettsville on 14 September 1888 for the murder of Coxe.
